# Review: three IA drifts in 05-stress-ia-drift

| # | Finding | ID | agent_risk | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Permission IA Drift on `/admin` (admin / manager / owner) | crime_00001 | **0.59** | **Block merge** |
| 2 | Parallel destination `/admin/billing-plans` ↔ `/billing-plans` | crime_00006 | 0.48 | **Warn** |
| 3 | Docs reference `iaq teams / workspace / refresh` that bin doesn't advertise | crime_00005 | 0.51 | **Warn** |

## 1. Permission IA Drift — block merge
`docs/routes.md` describes one role for `/admin`, `src/nav.ts:6` gates the link on another, and `src/routes/admin.ts` uses three literals (`admin`, `manager`, `owner`) across lines 2/4/9. Three sources of truth for an authorization boundary is the dangerous shape — an agent told to "let managers into admin" will edit whichever file it sees first and leave the others stale, producing either an over-permissive nav (link visible to users who 403 on click) or an under-permissive guard (silent dead end). Block until one canonical permission check is picked and the other two surfaces consume it.

## 2. Parallel Destination — warn
`src/routes/admin/billing-plans.ts` and `src/routes/billing-plans.ts` share the `billing`/`plan` tokens and have **no nav, doc, or import link between them** (crime_00006 evidence + the two orphan findings crime_00007/crime_00008 confirm both are unreachable). That's a warn, not a block: both are currently orphaned, so neither is a live user flow, but if either gets wired up an agent will likely edit only the one they found. Document which is canonical before linking either.

## 3. Docs Reference Missing Command — warn
`docs/routes.md` lines 23/27/31 reference `iaq teams`, `iaq workspace`, `iaq refresh`; `package.json` only advertises `get` and `list`. Agents following the doc hit "command not found" — annoying but self-revealing at runtime. Warn so the doc is fixed in the same PR, but it can't silently corrupt behavior the way crime_00001 can.

## Why crime_00001 carries the highest agent risk
Two reasons beyond the 0.59 score:

1. **Boundary kind.** It's an authorization boundary. The other two drifts produce broken links or stale docs — failure modes that surface on the next run. A permission drift produces *silent* behavioral skew: a role token added to the guard but not the nav still works, just inconsistently, and the inconsistency is exactly the gap an agent reading one file will fail to close.
2. **Three diverging tokens, not two.** `admin`, `manager`, `owner` aren't synonyms — they're a hierarchy. An agent picking the "wrong" canonical token doesn't just rename, it changes who can do what. crime_00006 has two overlapping routes (binary choice); crime_00005 has missing commands (detectable). crime_00001 has a three-way semantic conflict that won't throw at runtime.

Worth flagging that crime_00002 (Missing Agent Context, 0.54) compounds all three — no `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `SKILL.md` means an agent has no canonical pointer telling it which permission token, which route, or which command surface is authoritative. Fixing crime_00002 alongside crime_00001 would be cheap insurance.
